Thirty-seven comments

Does anyone have the name for this tune? It is the tune which comes after “For the Sake of Old Decency” in the reel set played by Mícheál Ó Raghallaigh and Danny O’Mahoney on Comhaltas Live: http://comhaltas.ie/music/detail/comhaltaslive_227_4_micheal_o_raghallaigh_and_danny_omahoney

Andrew McNamara and Padraic Mac Donnchadha also play this on “Maiden Voyage,” pairing it with “For the Sake of Old Decency.” It’s obviously related to a fairly common reel, The Steampacket.

↳ Posted by slainte on October 14th, 2007.

↳ Posted by niall_kenny on March 8th, 2015.

Brendan McMahon’s, X:4

This setting comes from Pat Mitchell’s book “The Dance Music of Willie Clancy” (1976) and is titled there as “The Mountain Lark”. Clearly it’s a major setting of the same tune, previously posted in dorian/minor settings. I think this gives more weight to the tune title being “The Mountain Lark” on this page.

Perhaps they’re all settings of The Steampacket? :)

↳ Posted by Jeremy on July 17th, 2022.

Tulla Moondance

Based on Seán Smyth’s playing on The Blue Fiddle (https://thesession.org/recordings/366). He plays it slowly with some interesting (new age?) accompaniment. It is modal, with (to my ears) a Clare sound; I can almost hear Martin Hayes playing it. The tune is related to the Steampacket, https://thesession.org/tunes/690. Maybe there’s a better name for it?

↳ Posted by brailsford on October 28th, 2022.

Tulla Moondance, X:10

From Holly Geraghty and John Roche’s excellent CD Ceolmhar (https://thesession.org/recordings/3286). They call the tune The Steampacket (to which it is clearly related) but it is so different to the usual (majorish) settings that it belongs here. Their setting is almost identical to Seán Smyth’s in the first part, and it follows his in outline in the turn. (Once the reel is brought down to Ddor)
Of course the first part is similar in a few bars to the turn of The Beauty Spot (https://thesession.org/tunes/1270) and Sollus Lillis’s Reel (https://thesession.org/tunes/4001)

↳ Posted by birlibirdie on April 27th, 2025.

The Mountain Lark, X:12

This is a setting of The mountain kark, recirded uneer that name by Kevin Ceawford in 2012 as a slow reel. (In a really lovely, mellow set plqyed before Jack in the box)

Kevin plays it in F on the Bb flute, I believe, which, effectively is A in D-notation.

He adds one or two variations, no more.
It’s a really lovely set and I’m going to learn this version (which is in keeping with the ones already posted above, including the abc’s, but has a gentle yet lively, laid back yet strong, feel to it. Recommanded listening.)

↳ Posted by birlibirdie on May 2nd, 2025.

Re: The Mountain Lark

The tune is wholy hexatonic in Kevin’s version (the 3rd degree gap is covered only once by a passing major 3rd); the other versions use a minor 3rd in the upper octave. This is enough to influence the sentiment.
